item.title: Man cover, 2nd August
item.description:
I am reporting significant damage and apparent movement/settlement to the driveway surrounding an inspection chamber/manhole. The chamber is located directly within the driveway outside my ground-floor maisonette in the London Borough of Bexley. As shown in the attached photographs, there are extensive and deep cracks radiating from the chamber, with sections of the concrete surface breaking apart and significant gaps developing around it. I am concerned that this may not simply be surface deterioration and that there could be a drainage defect, damaged chamber, subsidence or a void beneath the driveway. There has also previously been a blocked drain nearby containing a substantial amount of hair and debris. Please inspect the defect and establish who is responsible for the inspection chamber/drainage infrastructure and the associated damage. I would be grateful if this could be investigated before any repairs are carried out to the driveway, as I am concerned that simply filling the cracks may not resolve the underlying problem. I have attached photographs showing both the overall location and the extent of the cracking. Please treat this as a potential drainage/subsidence issue rather than simply a cosmetic defect to the driveway.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Park Mead, Blendon, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
